record.tranche_reason: The post comments on Anthropic's SAE feature interpretations and compares feature lists, but does not test individual-neuron polysemanticity or any listed version's neuron-level claim.
record.gate_note: The post reports two author analyses of SAE features, not individual neurons; these are recorded as findings that fit no version. Anthropic's reported correlation results and other results from the cited paper are not counted as this post's results.
record.test_reason: The post comments on Anthropic's SAE report. Its own analyses cover SAE features (Golden Gate activation split, 1M→34M feature recurrence) and a random-correlation simulation. None measures how often individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs, or the causes or measurement-dependence of neuron polysemanticity.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The author argues that naming SAE features by their top activations overstates interpretability and that SAEs do not consistently recover specific features. Add a third point: the author argues feature–neuron correlations near 0.3 are far above chance, contrary to Anthropic's reading.
record.recipe_differences: The post is commentary and analysis of Anthropic's SAE report, not a reproduction of the neuron-measurement method.
record.method_sensitivity: For the Golden Gate Bridge SAE feature, interpretation changes with activation level: the author says the high-activation cases fit the name better than median active instances.

fits_no_version.finding: The Golden Gate Bridge SAE feature fits its name mainly at high activations, estimated at <10% of its activations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature names drawn from top activations may describe only a minority of active instances.

fits_no_version.finding: 7 of 22 listed 1M-SAE safety features were judged to recur in related form in the 34M SAE.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features are not consistently recovered across dictionary sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: The author's simulation of random feature–neuron correlations never exceeded about 0.02. The author argues that Anthropic's max correlations near 0.3 indicate features correlate with neurons far beyond chance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features correlate with individual neurons far more than chance, even if not strongly in absolute terms.

record.problems: The Golden Gate Bridge proportion is an eyeballed estimate from a graph, with no reported uncertainty. The feature-recurrence tally is the author's manual matching of a list and is not an exhaustive search. The post does not directly test individual neurons.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results. Correlation figures discussed in the post are attributed to Anthropic's report and are not this post's own results.

untested.parts: No share of polysemantic MLP neurons measured.
No test of superposition as cause.
No test of initialization, regularization or noise as cause.
No reanalysis of canonical polysemantic neurons.
The activation-range argument is about SAE features, not about whether neurons count as polysemantic.

missing.what: Author's own simulation: max random feature–neuron correlation stays below 0.02, against Anthropic's reported ~0.3. This is not neuron polysemanticity, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.

record.verdict_notes: Rows_left_out wrongly treats all correlation content as Anthropic's results. The <0.02 simulation baseline is the author's own, though it bears on no version. The comments (e.g., Logan Riggs citing monosemantic neurons) are cited opinions, not results.

versions.untested_parts: No image-classifier neurons or mixed image inputs are measured.
No transformer MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts are measured.
No test of superposition or capacity pressure as a cause of polysemanticity.
No test of initialization, regularization, or training noise as a cause.
No comparison of activation functions, architectures, or regularization for neuron polysemanticity or performance.
The post questions interpretations of SAE features at different activation levels, but does not investigate canonical polysemantic neurons or establish that neuron mixtures share a feature.
The activation-range discussion concerns SAE features, not whether individual neurons count as polysemantic under different measurements or explanation scores.

rows.subject: Claude 3 Sonnet (SAE features; feature named Golden Gate Bridge)
rows.operation_detail: Eyeballed how often the feature's active instances appear relevant to the Golden Gate Bridge at different activation levels.
rows.measure: Share of feature activations that are relevant to the Golden Gate Bridge
rows.value: The author estimates the split is at least 90/10, possibly 99/1; fewer than 10% of activations are described as the high-activation cases where the feature is related to the Golden Gate Bridge.
rows.locator: A Feature Isn't Its Highest Activating Examples
rows.note: The author says the feature corresponds to the bridge at very high activation, but is irrelevant to the bridge on a median active instance, by the cited autointerpretability metric. This is an author estimate based on an eyeballed graph, not a neuron result.
rows.check: This concerns an SAE feature's activation distribution, not neurons, so no version applies. The state 'partial' has no version to be judged against. The value is an eyeballed estimate from Anthropic's graph with no uncertainty.

rows.subject: Claude 3 Sonnet (1M and 34M SAEs)
rows.operation_detail: Tallied whether listed safety-relevant features in the 1M SAE had a related counterpart in the 34M SAE.
rows.measure: Number of listed 1M SAE features judged to recur in related form in the 34M SAE
rows.value: 7/22 recurred; 15/22 did not, according to the author's tally.
rows.locator: Finding Specific Features; tally of More Safety Relevant Features
rows.note: The tally concerns whether SAE features recur across SAE sizes; it does not measure polysemantic neurons.
rows.check: This concerns SAE feature recurrence across dictionary sizes, not neuron polysemanticity, so the state 'observed' has no version referent. The tally is the author's manual match against a list that may not be exhaustive.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
